title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls and utilization reporting (v8)
author: Aisha Patel
description: This PR enhances Dedicated fleet autoscaling by tightening burst controls, adding throughput guarantee configuration, and improving utilization reporting surface area for the Console and Metrics pipelines. Motivation: customers running mixed-latency workloads were seeing uneven burst behavior and poor observability on short-lived traffic spikes which caused SLAs to be missed during ingress surges. Changes include: 1) deterministic burst window logic with configurable sliding-window and token-bucket fallback, 2) new throughput_guarantee config per pool that reserves a baseline vGPU capacity for critical routes, 3) expanded utilization metrics (utilization_normalized, burst_consumption, baseline_reserved) exported to Prometheus with stable label names, 4) Console UI additions for configuring burst policies and visualizing burst consumption, 5) migration script to backfill historical utilization metrics and a graceful rollout path for existing Dedicated clusters. Backwards compatibility: old burst settings remain supported but map to the new token-bucket parameters during migration. Testing: unit, integration, and canary perf runs against a 120-node Dedicated staging fleet showed 18% lower SLA violations under bursty load and stable long-tail latency. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and metrics dashboards.

review_comments: Tom Nguyen: The sliding-window approach looks good but can we bound memory usage for long windows? Suggest adding a sampling cap and summarization to avoid O(window) memory on large fleets.
Aisha Patel: Added summarization and sampling cap; documented the tradeoff in code comments and the docs page. The implementation keeps 1s resolution and summarizes to minute buckets after 5 minutes.
Priya Rao: We need a clear migration path for clusters that relied on previous burst heuristics. Will this change cause sudden capacity shifts after upgrade?

Aisha Patel: Migration script included to map old configs to token-bucket parameters. Default rollout keeps legacy-equivalent settings unless admin opts into strict throughput guarantees. Added notes in docs and a CLI dry-run mode.
Luis Martinez: CI integration showed a flaky test 'autoscaler_throttle_test' failing in the first run. Can we stabilize?
Aisha Patel: Fixed race in test harness by adding deterministic clock in tests and added additional assertions. Re-ran CI and green on subsequent runs.
ci_checks: perf/canary: pass (canary against staging-120-node showing 18% fewer SLA violations)
flaky-tests: autoscaler_throttle_test failed on first run, rerun passed
merge_summary: Squash-merged into main. Migration SQL runs and a helm values bump were applied. Admins should run the included migration in maintenance windows to backfill metrics names. Default behavior remains backward compatible unless throughput_guarantee is explicitly set.
release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler burst controls and utilization reporting. New throughput_guarantee config allows reserving baseline capacity per pool. Console shows burst consumption and normalized utilization. Migration script included to backfill metrics. See docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md for rollout steps and examples. Impact: reduced SLA violations during short spikes for most workloads.
notes_for_sre: Deploy sequence: 1) deploy service changes to Dedicated control plane, 2) run migration SQL against observability store, 3) bump helm dedicated-values to opt into stricter defaults if desired, 4) enable new console flags. Monitor autoscaler.burst_consumption and autoscaler.utilization_normalized for 1 hour post-rollout.
user_facing_changes: Admins can now configure per-pool throughput_guarantee and view burst consumption in Console. Metric names changed to stable forms; migration will create aliases for old names for 30 days.
testing_notes: Includes new unit and integration tests that exercise token-bucket fallback and throughput guarantee enforcement. Canary performed on a 120-node staging fleet with synthetic burst workload used in ENG-1198.
